solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fungus problem around hotel pantry perhaps

indicators.note: around here means the word for a problem is turned the other way round

parts.note: a sum is a problem set in arithmetic
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a pantry is one example of a room

explanation.surface: A trouble with the hotel's larder, possibly involving mould.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns the problem word back to front; 'pantry perhaps' is an example of a room, hence the 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: The mushroom is the best-known fruiting body of a fungus, so it is an example.

clue.text: Andy repositioned second live wire

indicators.note: repositioned says the letters of Andy are moved into a new order

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second, as in 'wait a mo'

explanation.surface: Andy has been moved, and now a lively character takes his place.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is an energetic, forceful person, the same idiom as a live wire.

clue.text: Battle station

explanation.surface: Battle station reads as a military post ready for combat.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to Wellington's famous victory and to a busy London rail terminus.

clue.text: Father interrupts street quarrel

indicators.note: interrupts means one piece breaks into the middle of the other

parts.note: Pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Dad steps into a row happening out on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A spat is a petty quarrel, a near-synonym for a squabble.

clue.text: In French, Hugo managed adequately

parts.note: en is the French word for in

indicators.note: managed suggests the letters of Hugo are handled and worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Speaking French, Victor Hugo coped well enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Enough as an adverb means sufficiently, to a satisfactory degree.

clue.text: Conceal British identity somewhat

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Keep your British nationality a little bit quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: To hide something is to keep it out of sight, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Landing-place is crucial, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is identified by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: key means crucial, as in a key point

explanation.surface: Rumour says the landing spot is vital.
explanation.definitionFit: A quay is a stone wharf where boats moor and unload, a place to land.

clue.text: Arranged index on a couple of pages: it may be at back of book

definitions.text: it may be at back of book

indicators.note: on in an across clue sends the rearranged index after the pages, written next

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for page, so PP is two pages

indicators.note: Arranged says the letters of index are put into a different order

explanation.surface: An index laid out over two pages, the sort of thing found at the end of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arranged' reworks the letters of index, and the result sits after the pages.
explanation.definitionFit: An appendix is supplementary material placed at the end of a book.

clue.text: Vehicle turned into the ancient region

indicators.note: into says one piece is placed within the other
turned means the word for vehicle is read backwards

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A vehicle turned and headed into an old territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses the vehicle, and 'into' puts it within the word 'the', which looks like part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrace was a historical land in the south-east Balkans, known from antiquity.

clue.text: Hairpiece lifted on Owen's head in part of golf course

indicators.note: in says the next pieces are placed within the golf word

parts.note: the tee is the area a golf hole is played from

indicators.note: on in an across clue means one piece follows after the other
head points to the first letter of Owen's

parts.note: lifted means up, raised

explanation.surface: Owen's wig flies up off his head on the golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: A toupee is a small wig worn to cover a bald patch.

clue.text: Grounded bird no longer parties

parts.note: a do is a party, so two parties are two DOs

explanation.surface: The flightless bird is gone, and so are the parties.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'parties' calls for the party word twice.
explanation.definitionFit: The dodo was a flightless bird that became extinct, so it exists no longer.

clue.text: Expression of hilarity from female offspring showing different face

indicators.note: a different face means the front letter of the word is swapped for another

parts.note: a daughter is female offspring

explanation.surface: A girl's changed expression shows she is amused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing different face' swaps the first letter: D gives way to L.
explanation.definitionFit: Laughter is the sound people make when something amuses them.

clue.text: University study about diet strangely not corrected

indicators.note: about here means the study word is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: a den is a study, a private room for work

indicators.note: strangely says the combined letters are jumbled into an odd order

explanation.surface: A university study of an odd diet was never revised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses the study word, and 'strangely' reorders DIET into ITED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unedited has not been revised or checked by an editor.

clue.text: Sort of tea regularly gorged inside ahead of time

indicators.note: inside says the picked letters sit within the word for ahead of time

parts.note: early means ahead of time

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of gorged is taken

explanation.surface: Someone stuffed themselves with tea well before teatime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes G, R, E from GORGED.
explanation.definitionFit: Earl Grey is a black tea flavoured with bergamot oil, one kind of tea.

clue.text: One who eats everything, having drunk more vino

indicators.note: drunk says the letters of more vino are staggered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who eats anything has also downed more wine.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnivore is an animal or person feeding on both plants and meat.

clue.text: Line on certain maps represents old pub

parts.note: is can mean represents, as in 'this dot is London'
a bar is a place to drink, like a pub

explanation.surface: A line on a map marks an old public house.
explanation.definitionFit: An isobar is a line on weather charts joining points of equal air pressure.

clue.text: Mother concerned with horse

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A mother who is interested in horses.
explanation.definitionFit: A mare is a female horse, so a particular kind of horse.

clue.text: Simple poem in manuscript ending in basket

indicators.note: in says the poem sits inside the manuscript letters

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

indicators.note: ending in points to the last letter of basket

explanation.surface: A plain poem written out by hand ends up in the waste basket.
explanation.definitionFit: Modest can mean plain and unpretentious, as in a modest house.

clue.text: Noted a tailless rodent after initially following

indicators.note: after says the next pieces come behind the first letter
initially points to the first letter of following
tailless means the last letter of the rodent is cut off

parts.note: a mouse is a rodent

explanation.surface: Someone noticed a mouse without a tail trailing along behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Famous and noted both describe someone well known and celebrated.

clue.text: First male attorney to stand up in the morning

indicators.note: to stand up in a down clue means the letters are read from the bottom upward

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, a US prosecutor
AM stands for ante meridiem, the morning

explanation.surface: The lead male lawyer must rise early in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to stand up' turns DA into AD.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, Adam is the first man God created.

clue.text: Look for king buried under religious grounds

indicators.note: buried under in a down clue means the king goes below the other piece

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese, the area of their authority
K is the abbreviation for king in chess

explanation.surface: Searching for a monarch interred beneath church land.
explanation.definitionFit: To seek is to look for, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Shade during excavation nil

parts.note: in can mean during, as in 'in the morning'
a dig is an archaeological excavation
O stands for nil, zero

explanation.surface: A colour turns up while digging up nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is a deep blue-violet colour, one shade of the spectrum.

clue.text: Asian involved Sean in joke

indicators.note: in says the jumbled name sits within the joke word

parts.note: a jape is a practical joke

indicators.note: involved means the letters of Sean are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: An Asian man got Sean caught up in a prank.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese person comes from Japan, so is an Asian.

clue.text: Casual geezer repeatedly showing heart somewhere in Egypt

indicators.note: showing heart, done repeatedly, takes the central letters of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A laid-back bloke keeps wearing his heart on his sleeve somewhere in Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: Each six-letter word gives its middle pair: SU and EZ. A geezer is British slang for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Suez is a port city in Egypt, at the southern end of the canal.
